name: Traditional Palm Calabash (Kibuyu)
description: A dried and polished gourd traditionally used for carrying fresh water and mnazi (palm sap) during village gatherings.
historical_note: Palm wine tapping (mnazi) was central to Giriama hospitality and ritual economy. The British attempted to suppress it to force the population into wage labor.

name: Kaya Medicinal Pouch
description: A fragrant bundle of coastal coastal wild roots gathered from the sacred forest of Kaya Fungo.
historical_note: Kaya elders used sacred botanicals for ritual purification, healing, and preparing warriors and councils before major communal decisions.

name: British Colonial Labor Decree
description: A printed notice stamped with the British East Africa Protectorate seal, demanding hut taxes and male labor recruits.
historical_note: In 1913, Assistant District Commissioner Arthur Champion enforced harsh poll taxes and labor quotas, prompting Mekatilili wa Menza's direct defiance.
